about.summary: I’m a final-year Electrical Engineering student at Adeleke University and an independent engineer building at the intersection of software and physical systems.
narrative: My projects span real-time networking, blockchain infrastructure, AI agents, embedded electronics, and telecommunications. I enjoy taking unfamiliar problems apart, learning the underlying principles, and building systems I can test and improve.

I’m looking for ambitious engineering teams where I can contribute as a junior engineer, learn from strong technical peers, and work on problems that reward curiosity and rigorous execution. Outside formal work, I intend to keep building independent projects and documenting my research.

flagships.title: World of Nads
flagships.subtitle: Real-Time Multiplayer Systems
flagships.description: A browser-based 3D multiplayer arena game. Built with Godot compiled to WebAssembly for seamless zero-install delivery, backed by an authoritative Rust WebSocket multiplayer server running 20Hz deterministic state synchronization, and Monad-focused EVM on-chain prize distribution.

caseStudy.problem: Delivering a fast 3D multiplayer arena game directly inside the browser without requiring external game launchers, while maintaining smooth real-time state synchronization across 20 concurrent players in volatile network environments.
caseStudy.difficulty: Bridging three distinct domains in real time: the Godot WebAssembly graphics runtime, the browser JavaScript environment (wallet authentication & UI), and a low-latency Rust WebSocket backend server, all under tight client-side memory and CPU constraints.
caseStudy.personalContribution: Independently built the game client in Godot, authored 3D game assets and mechanics, implemented client-side interpolation, built the 20Hz Rust WebSocket state server, and integrated Monad EVM smart contracts for prize distribution.

components.name: Browser Client
components.desc: Godot 4 WASM/WebGL canvas handling physics, input capture, and local interpolation

components.name: Interop Bridge
components.desc: Lightweight JS boundary relaying wallet signatures and WebSocket frames without DOM overhead

components.name: Rust Server Engine
components.desc: 20Hz authoritative tick loop, spatial partitioning, delta compression, and heartbeat monitoring

components.name: Monad Settlement
components.desc: Smart contracts executing deterministic match entry escrow and verifiable prize disbursement

tradeoffs: Optimistic client prediction vs strict server validation: prioritized visual responsiveness on standard 60Hz displays while keeping collision validation authoritative on the Rust server.
Compact binary WebSocket frames vs JSON: stripped serialization overhead, reducing packet payload sizes by over 60%.
caseStudy.hardestBug: During early testing, browser frame rates plummeted from 60 FPS to under 12 FPS on lower-spec hardware. Profiling traced the bottleneck to frequent per-frame function calls across the Godot-WASM to JavaScript React boundary. Resolved by decoupling rendering from network updates, batching bridge calls at 20Hz, and passing contiguous typed arrays.
caseStudy.verifiedStatus: Publicly playable at worldofnads.xyz. Monad-focused EVM architecture (Solana legacy references removed).
caseStudy.nextSteps: Implement client-side rollback lag compensation buffers and optimize initial WASM bundle size with progressive texture loading.

flagships.title: EEG Communication Headset
flagships.subtitle: Embedded Systems Experiment
flagships.description: An experimental hardware and firmware investigation exploring an affordable, wearable communication-support interface for non-speaking users. Integrates forehead dry EEG electrodes, a TGAM biosensing frontend, an ESP32 microcontroller, audio amplification, and bone-conduction transducers.

caseStudy.problem: Commercial brain-computer and assistive speech interfaces cost thousands of dollars, require wet conductive pastes, or depend on continuous desktop tethering, placing them out of reach for everyday mobility in resource-constrained environments.
caseStudy.difficulty: Scalp biosignals sit in the microvolt range (10-100 μV) and are easily corrupted by ocular blinks, jaw clenches (EMG), and 50Hz environmental powerline hum. Achieving reproducible, intentional user triggers on an embedded microcontroller without false alarms requires disciplined filtering and FreeRTOS task prioritization.
caseStudy.personalContribution: Designed the circuit schematic and breadboard layout, implemented dual-core FreeRTOS firmware in C++ on the ESP32, developed the ThinkGear UART serial packet decoder with strict checksum validation, and configured the audio amplification circuit driving bone-conduction transducers.

components.name: Scalp Dry Electrodes
components.desc: Single-point Fp1 forehead electrode with earlobe ground and reference clips

components.name: TGAM Biosensing Frontend
components.desc: Hardware pre-amplifier, 50Hz notch filter, and 12-bit ADC outputting ThinkGear packets over UART

components.name: ESP32 Firmware Layer
components.desc: Core 0 consumes 57600 baud serial stream; Core 1 evaluates intentional threshold events and state transitions

components.name: Audio Synthesis & Transducer
components.desc: DAC/PWM tone generator into PAM8403 amplifier driving a bone-conduction transducer

auditStatus.hardwareAssembled: Benchtop breadboard and perfboard test bench established for signal validation, serial telemetry, and audio triggering.
auditStatus.firmwareImplemented: UART packet parser validating 0xAA 0xAA sync bytes and packet checksums; real-time extraction of Poor Signal Quality, Attention, and raw wave packets; dual-threshold state machine for intentional blink detection.
auditStatus.testedResults: Verified packet integrity at 57,600 baud with zero buffer overrun across 30-minute stress runs; confirmed audible feedback delivered via bone conduction against temporal bone.
auditStatus.limitationsAndHonestScope: Does NOT decode continuous speech, arbitrary thoughts, or complex linguistic sentences. The system operates strictly as an intentional state/event trigger (e.g., deliberate consecutive blinks or concentrated focus thresholds) mapped to discrete assistive audio cues.

caseStudy.nextSteps: Transition from perfboard to a custom two-layer PCB; print a 3D ergonomic adjustable headset headband; incorporate adaptive baseline drift rejection.

flagships.title: Cellular Fingerprint Positioning System
flagships.subtitle: Telecommunications Research
flagships.description: My final-year Electrical Engineering capstone project at Adeleke University. Investigating position estimation algorithms in urban and indoor environments using cellular signal fingerprints (GSM/LTE RSSI, Cell ID, LAC, and Timing Advance) where satellite GPS signals are severely attenuated or unavailable.

caseStudy.problem: Satellite GPS signals suffer dramatic attenuation, multipath distortion, and power drain inside concrete buildings and high-density urban areas. Asset tracking and emergency location require an alternative positioning mechanism utilizing existing terrestrial cellular infrastructure.
caseStudy.difficulty: Cellular Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) exhibits high temporal and spatial variance caused by shadow fading, structural multipath, and dynamic network load balancing, rendering naive geometric trilateration error-prone.
caseStudy.personalContribution: Formulated the research methodology, assembled the hardware survey logging rig (microcontroller + cellular modem running AT commands), gathered empirical RSSI vectors across campus reference points, and implemented baseline fingerprint matching algorithms.

components.name: Base Station Array
components.desc: Multiple commercial cell towers (serving and neighbor cells) broadcasting GSM/LTE beacon channels

components.name: Logging Test Rig
components.desc: Hardware transceiver interrogating modem registers (AT+CSQ, AT+CREG, AT+COPS) with timestamped coordinates

components.name: Spatial Radio Map (Offline)
components.desc: Calibrated database associating reference locations (X, Y) with multi-dimensional RSSI fingerprint vectors

components.name: Pattern Matching Engine (Online)
components.desc: K-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) and probabilistic matching determining estimated position from unknown vectors

featuresLogged: Neighbor Cell IDs and relative signal levels
researchDetails.algorithmExploration: Benchmarking Euclidean k-NN vs Mahalanobis distance and Bayesian probabilistic modeling to handle signal fluctuation.
researchDetails.currentStage: Hardware logging rig calibrated; offline grid sampling ongoing across predefined outdoor-to-indoor transition zones at Adeleke University; constructing baseline error CDF.
researchDetails.limitations: Accuracy is bounded by cell tower density and environmental dynamics (weather, structural movement). The work is actively ongoing as part of my graduating degree requirements.

caseStudy.nextSteps: Complete grid cross-validation, evaluate Weighted k-NN against Gaussian Process Regression, and document empirical Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) positioning error curves for thesis presentation.

flagships.title: Know Your Protocol (KYP)
flagships.subtitle: On-Chain Accountability
flagships.description: A protocol accountability platform built around commitments, stakes, and verifiable follow-through. Users research protocols through AI pipelines, lock economic stakes into smart contracts, and have their follow-through verified across EVM protocols without custom event signatures.

caseStudy.problem: Web3 researchers and protocol contributors routinely make commitments to test or research protocols, yet lack verifiable mechanisms for economic follow-through. Existing tools rely on centralized human attestations or rigid, protocol-specific smart contract hooks.
caseStudy.difficulty: Creating a protocol-agnostic verification system that inspects a user's on-chain activity across any EVM protocol without requiring custom event signatures or proprietary ABI decoders, while operating a zero-cost autonomous verification heartbeat.
caseStudy.personalContribution: Architected the complete system: Svelte 5 frontend, smart contract commitment logic with automatic stake verification and slashing, a protocol-agnostic on-chain event scanner using indexed getLogs, and a zero-cost heartbeat worker architecture.

components.name: Research Engine
components.desc: Dual-tier AI pipeline (FlashResearcher + DeepResearcher via Gemini) synthesizing protocol parameters

components.name: Commitment Contract
components.desc: Solidity vault locking user stakes under a 9-day, 3-strike programmable accountability model

components.name: Heartbeat Daemon
components.desc: Zero-cost heartbeat worker triggering periodic verification passes without paid subscription cron services

components.name: Event Filter Engine
components.desc: Dynamic getLogs indexer scanning raw block logs for address interaction regardless of contract ABI

tradeoffs: Protocol-agnostic log queries vs custom ABI decoders: chosen to allow users to verify engagement with ANY arbitrary new EVM smart contract on Monad without requiring pre-compiled contract artifacts.
Adaptive block-time estimation vs fixed timestamps: dynamically calculates inspection intervals from network block rate rather than hardcoded assumptions.
caseStudy.hardestBug: Eliminating RPC rate limits while scanning wide block ranges across multi-network environments (Monad Testnet and Mainnet). Solved by implementing exponential backoff with adaptive chunk size throttling in the custom getLogs worker.
caseStudy.verifiedStatus: Publicly deployed and verified on GitHub; recognized during the BuildAnything Spark Hackathon.
caseStudy.nextSteps: Add multi-sig commitment vaults and extend verification heuristics to cross-chain LayerZero messaging events.

research.title: Cellular Signal Fingerprinting for GPS-Denied Localization
research.question: What localization accuracy and error bounds can be achieved indoors using opportunistic GSM/LTE multi-cell RSSI vectors without deploying custom anchor hardware?
research.context: Traditional satellite GPS signals degrade rapidly inside concrete buildings and industrial environments. Cellular fingerprinting leverages existing radio infrastructure by mapping unique multipath patterns.
research.methodology: Two-phase system: (1) An empirical offline survey collecting multi-cell RSSI, Cell ID, LAC, and Timing Advance across mapped test coordinates using AT-command modems. (2) An online positioning engine comparing real-time vectors via k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) and Bayesian probability models.
research.currentFindings: Signal variance on indoor corridors averages ±4.2 dBm under stationary conditions; multi-cell vector fusion significantly suppresses single-tower ambiguity.
research.openQuestions: Quantifying error degradation under heavy human movement and evaluating how dynamic weather conditions alter 900MHz/1800MHz propagation contours.

research.title: Low-Cost Biosignal Interfaces: Artifact Filtering on ESP32 Microcontrollers
research.question: How reliably can an entry-level dry-electrode EEG frontend be filtered in real-time on an embedded dual-core microcontroller to detect deliberate trigger events without false positives?
research.context: Commercial brain-computer interfaces are prohibitively expensive for assistive care in developing nations. Integrating commercial-off-the-shelf ASICs like the NeuroSky TGAM with an ESP32 offers an ultra-low-cost pathway.
research.methodology: Configured 57600-baud UART streaming with FreeRTOS task isolation; Core 0 handles checksum validation and 512Hz raw wave buffering; Core 1 runs dynamic thresholding to separate deliberate intentional blinks from ambient EMG jaw-clenching noise.
research.currentFindings: Dual-blink intentional gestures produce distinct high-amplitude biphasic spikes (>200μV equivalent) that can be reliably classified with rolling standard deviation windowing (>94% classification precision in bench calibration).
research.openQuestions: Integrating bone-conduction audio back-EMF isolation to prevent feedback loop coupling into the scalp electrode reference.

research.title: State Consistency & Reorg Recovery in High-Throughput EVM Networks
research.question: In sub-second block architectures with frequent micro-reorganizations, how can off-chain indexers maintain 100% deterministic state consistency without prohibitive multi-block finality lag?
research.context: High-throughput chains like Monad execute state rapidly, but asynchronous peer gossiping can cause temporary fork divergence that corrupts off-chain indexing databases if state is written immediately.
research.methodology: Implemented a triple-RPC quorum polling engine with a rolling FIFO block buffer. When parent-hash mismatch is detected across nodes, the indexer triggers an automated retroactive unwind, reversing mutated state up to the common ancestor before re-indexing.
research.currentFindings: A 12-block rewind buffer eliminates 100% of temporary branch corruption under network jitter without requiring manual administrative intervention.
research.openQuestions: Extending the consensus quorum engine to zero-knowledge state proof validation for instant finality verification.

writing.title: Communicating in Functions
writing.summary: On engineering as communication — and why a function is just an idea precise enough to survive without its author. Examines interface boundaries, predictable contracts, and writing software that communicates intent clearly to both compilers and future teammates.

writing.title: Success Is 90% Luck and Informed Guessing
writing.summary: A probability framework for luck, consistency, and what to do when life hands you a defective die. Exploring Bayesian priors, increasing personal surface area for serendipity, and how technical builders turn probabilistic outcomes in their favor through relentless shipping.
